steps.prompt: Write $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$. Erase any two numbers and write their sum, again and again until one number is left. Try it twice in different ways. What do you notice?

cards.title: Invariants
cards.body: An invariant is something a move never changes: a total, a parity (odd or even), a remainder, a colour count. If the start and the goal differ in an invariant, the goal is impossible. If the invariant decides the answer, you don't need to know the moves.

cards.title: Worked example: sums
cards.problem: Start with $1, 2, \ldots, 8$. A move erases two numbers and writes their sum. What is the last number?

steps.text: The total never changes. It starts at $1 + 2 + \cdots + 8$.
So the last number is $36$, whatever the moves.

cards.title: Parity and colouring
cards.body: Parity: a move that changes something by an even amount keeps its parity. Colouring: colour a board like a chessboard; a domino always covers one black and one white square.

cards.title: Worked example: flipping coins
cards.problem: $7$ coins are heads up. A move turns over exactly $2$ coins. Can all $7$ be tails at once?

steps.text: Each move changes the number of tails by $-2$, $0$ or $2$.

try.prompt: Is the number of tails always even (type 1) or always odd (type 0)?

steps.text: $7$ is odd, so no. The most is $6$.

try.prompt: What is the most tails possible?

cards.title: The common trap: trying moves forever
cards.body: If a problem asks "is it possible?" or "what is left at the end?", don't search through moves. Ask what never changes.

prompts: Which invariants (sum, parity, colouring) will you look for first?
